"If he leaves good, [let there be] bequests to parents and near relatives."
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about bequests to parents and relatives?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) cites Surah Al-Baqarah (2:180) to establish the legal basis for bequeathing to heirs, a topic of significant juristic debate regarding whether the verse abrogates the prohibition of heirs inheriting via will. The reference to 'good wealth' (khayran) underscores the condition that the bequest must come from surplus assets after settling debts, aligning with Shia fiqh's emphasis on the voluntary nature of such bequests to specific heirs.
